I can’t search the web from here, and I won’t fabricate sources or make up links. I also can’t claim any source “proves” that remote work always increases productivity — reputable research shows mixed results depending on job type, measurement, management, and context.

What I can do now
- Explain briefly what the real research generally shows (balanced summary from my training through 2024).
- Give three well-known, verifiable studies/reports you can look up (I won’t invent URLs). Each entry includes a short description and a suggested search query you can paste into Google or your library to find the original.
- Offer to fetch and cite these if you re-enable web tools or paste the documents.

Balanced summary (brief)
- Some controlled studies and company reports found measurable productivity gains from remote work in specific settings (e.g., call centers, knowledge work), driven by fewer interruptions, lower commute time, and flexible hours.
- Other studies show no change or declines in productivity for tasks requiring close collaboration, access to equipment, or when employees lack good home setups or managerial support.
- Net effect depends on the role, how productivity is measured (output vs. hours vs. quality), and organizational supports (technology, management practices, culture).

Three verifiable sources to check
1) Bloom et al., 2015 — "Does Working from Home Work? Evidence from a Chinese Experiment"
- Why check it: A randomized experiment at a Chinese travel agency that reported productivity gains for remote workers (often cited in debates about remote work productivity).
- Suggested search: Does Working from Home Work? Evidence from a Chinese Experiment Bloom Liang Roberts Ying 2015

2) Microsoft — Work/Work Trend Index reports (2020–2022)
- Why check it: Microsoft’s corporate reports and analyses of Teams/Office usage documented changes in meeting patterns, collaboration metrics, and company-reported productivity signals during the pandemic; they also discuss hybrid work trade-offs.
- Suggested search: Microsoft Work Trend Index 2021 productivity remote work

3) McKinsey / Harvard Business Review synthesis pieces on remote/hybrid work
- Why check them: McKinsey and HBR published evidence-based syntheses and surveys showing varied productivity outcomes and practical recommendations; these are useful for understanding nuance rather than absolute claims.
- Suggested searches:
  - McKinsey remote work productivity survey 2020 2021
  - Harvard Business Review remote work productivity research summary

If you’d like
- I can, without web access, expand the summary with more detail from my training-data knowledge (e.g., approximate effect sizes reported by some studies and typical caveats).
- Or, if you enable web access or paste the articles, I’ll retrieve and cite them precisely.
